name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: I'm applying for the Lifecycle Marketing Specialist role. Lifecycle work is the part of marketing I've spent the most time inside. At Solenzo I built a 20+ workflow system covering the full arc: capture, tagging and routing, qualification, booking with confirmations and reminders, no-show recovery, post-sale onboarding nurture, long-term reactivation, and automated review generation. I designed the segmentation and lifecycle stages underneath it, and I built the reporting that showed which stages were actually converting and which ones were quietly leaking.

Before that, most of my career was on the other side of the same problem. At Wix I onboarded and launched 25+ clients a month and led onboarding operations for a high-value portfolio, so activation and time-to-value are things I've owned by hand, not just automated. At Birdeye I built the training sequences and communication workflows that got a 15 to 20 partner network productive, and watched engagement data to catch adoption gaps before they became churn. Retaining all but one of that book came from the intervening, not from the sending.

On platforms I'm hands-on in HubSpot, Salesforce, and GoHighLevel, with real data-hygiene discipline behind the builds, because segmentation is only as good as the records under it. I also spend my working days building AI and agent systems, which is increasingly where lifecycle personalization is heading.
I'm in Arvada, so the Lakewood hybrid schedule is a short drive. I'd welcome the conversation.
